subject: Discovery recap: embeddings + rerank for SouthPoint Retail
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@southpointretail.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@southpointretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: embeddings + rerank for SouthPoint Retail

Hi Alicia / Daniel —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really useful conversation. Per our call, below is a short recap of what we heard, what success looks like for you, and proposed next steps for a short POC. Please flag anything I missed or want to correct.

Key pain points
- Current site search and recommendations often return stale or noisy results for long-tail SKUs (poor recall for new products).
- Relevance tuning in Elastic has hit diminishing returns; team wants vector similarity + reranking for top-K results.
- Cost and latency at scale are a hard constraint — need predictable unit economics as index grows.
\Current stack / constraints you shared
- Production vector DB: Pinecone (namespace: prod_catalog) — used for online lookups.
- Research: FAISS-based pipelines for offline experiments.
- Current catalog size ~35M SKUs (high-cardinality product attributes).
- Embedding dimension: 1536 (Open-embedding family).
\Success criteria (what will make a POC a win)
- Latency: 95th percentile for rerank (top-10) <= 75 ms end-to-end from query to sorted results.
- Quality: +10-15% CTR lift on recommended items in A/B vs current production model (measured on a held-out prompt set).
- Cost target: keep incremental production inference cost at or below your target (we discussed rough target of <$0.02 per query for the rerank step; will fine-tune in budgeting).
- Scalability: support ~35M vectors with nightly reindex and steady-state real-time ingestion of ~5k vectors/day.
\Observed / expected traffic patterns
- Average queries: ~120k similarity queries/day.
- Peak concurrency: ~200-300 q/s during promotions.
- Batch patterns: nightly full reindex, incremental hourly updates for price/availability changes (~1-2k vectors/hour).
\Proposed POC plan (2-3 weeks)
1) Kickoff & data handoff — you provide a representative sample export (we discussed a 1-5% sample or a 1M-vector slice) + top queries set.
2) Baseline integration — Redwood runs an evaluation against the sample using an embedding model (we'll propose open-embed-1536) and our reranking pipeline.
3) Latency tuning — iterate on batching/quantization and vector DB config (Pinecone namespace or a local FAISS replica) to hit latency SLOs.
4) Readout & next steps — quality and cost estimates for production rollout, recommended infra (hosted vs dedicated).
\Attachments: redwood-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal + POC scope)
\Next steps / asks
- Can you share a sample export (1M-vector slice or the CSV layout) and the top-queries test set?
- Confirm Slack contact (Alicia if ok) and preferred kickoff times next week.
\I’ll loop Rishi (SE) and Neha (CS) on technical follow-up. Thanks again — excited to partner.
\Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the call well. A few clarifications and details from our side:

- Confirming catalog is ~35M SKUs (includes inactive/backstock records we can filter).
- Pinecone is used in production (dense index for top-K). We also keep a nightly FAISS export for offline experiments.
- Typical ingestion: nightly full reindex of ~40M vectors (long job), plus continuous update stream ~5k vectors/day for new/changed SKUs.
- Query volume: ~120k similarity queries/day, peaks up to ~320 q/s during marketing peaks.
- Latency target: 95th <= 75ms for rerank (we measure from our web tier to final ranked response).
- Cost target: we'd like to keep incremental production cost for rerank under $0.02/query if possible — we know this depends on model choice and infra.
\I attached a small sample export and the data profile (spp-data-profile.csv) for the slice we discussed — it’s ~1.2M vectors and anonymized product IDs. Let me know if you need a different slice or a different schema.
\A couple of asks:
- Can Redwood outline whether you recommend running embeddings & rerank in-hosted (your managed infra) vs Dedicated for predictability? We’re sensitive to p95 latency variability.
- Would it help if we shared read-only Pinecone export access or would you prefer a static CSV export?
\Happy to kick off next Wednesday afternoon (Nov 2) — open to a shorter tech deep-dive ahead of the POC.
\Thanks,
Alicia
Head of Search & Recommendations | SouthPoint Retail

Hi Alicia / Daniel — looping in a few technical notes and a proposed POC checklist from our side. Great to see the sample — thanks.
\Technical notes / assumptions
- Model baseline: we’ll evaluate using an open-embed-1536 family (matching your 1536 dim) and compare against a small LLM-based reranker for top-10 scoring.
- Vector DB options for POC: we can point at your Pinecone namespace (read-only) for realistic latency, or stand up a FAISS replica in Redwood infra for controlled experiments. Both are useful: Pinecone for fidelity, FAISS for rapid iteration.
- Latency approach: target p95 <= 75 ms. We'll instrument end-to-end (client -> Redwood -> vector DB -> reranker). We typically get to p95 <= 60-90 ms depending on vector size and topology; we’ll tune batching, shard placement, and KV cache.
- Index sizing: 35M vectors (1536 dim) — we recommend initial quantization (8-bit or bfloat16) during inference to reduce memory footprint; we'll evaluate quality/regression.
\POC checklist / timeline (2 weeks)
1) Access & sample data (you to provide): 1M-vector slice OR read-only Pinecone export + top-queries file.
2) Baseline eval (3-4 days): run similarity + rerank on sample, measure latency and quality.
3) Tune & optimize (4-5 days): try quantization, batching, and small dedicated instance to hit p95 targets.
4) Readout & recommendations (1-2 days): produce a quality vs cost trade-off and recommended infra (hosted vs Dedicated).
\Ops ask: if you can share a time-limited read-only Pinecone export/link that would be easiest for realistic latency numbers. If that’s not possible, the CSV slice is fine — we’ll note the difference in fidelity.
\Alicia — if you can confirm the preferred data handoff method and a kickoff slot next week, we’ll schedule Rishi + Neha + infra lead.
\Thanks — Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
